summary: A Qode Interactive tutorial (June 2, 2021, by Sasa Stojanovic) explaining how to enqueue custom JavaScript and CSS in WordPress using wp_enqueue_script and wp_enqueue_style, with hooks, parameters, path functions, and examples for frontend, backend, and conditional loading. It also covers inline additions via wp_add_inline_script and wp_add_inline_style and notes the method suits advanced users. The article ends with a reader comment about a missing parenthesis in an example, which the author fixed.
one_line: Tutorial on enqueueing custom JavaScript and CSS in WordPress, covering hooks, parameters, frontend/backend loading, conditional enqueueing, and inline code.
key_facts: The article 'How to Enqueue Custom Scripts and Style Sheets in WordPress' was published June 2, 2021, by Sasa Stojanovic.
The wp_enqueue_script function has five parameters: $handle, $src, $deps, $ver, and $in_footer, and only $handle is mandatory.
The default value of $ver is false, which sets it to the current WordPress version; when set to null, no version is added.
The default value of $in_footer is 'false', meaning the script loads in the head; 'true' loads it before the closing body tag.
The wp_enqueue_style function also has five arguments, and its $media argument defaults to 'all'.
The wp_enqueue_scripts hook is intended for scripts and stylesheets affecting the frontend, while admin_enqueue_scripts is for the admin dashboard.
Filters edit the argument they are given and always need to return a value, whereas actions don't need to return a value.
get_template_directory_uri() returns the parent theme directory path without the trailing slash, and get_stylesheet_directory_uri() returns the child theme directory path.
plugins_url() accepts up to two parameters: the extra path and the full relative path of the file, noted by including __FILE__ as the second parameter.
wp_register_script only registers a script, while wp_enqueue_script both registers and enqueues it.
In the conditional example, the comment-reply script is enqueued only if is_singular(), comments_open(), and get_option('thread_comments') are all true, using the && operator.
wp_deregister_style is used to deregister a previously registered stylesheet so a new one can be enqueued under the same handle.
wp_add_inline_script takes three arguments, of which $handle and $data are required, and $position defaults to 'after'.
wp_add_inline_style takes two arguments, $handle and $data, and the stylesheet must be enqueued before it is used.
The article states that enqueueing is best for adding larger custom scripts and stylesheets but is an advanced-user method.
